operational.family_note: No registered FeatureFamily covers phase gradients along channel index, so the record carries no family.

measurement.definition: Mean absolute wrapped difference between adjacent channels in channel-index order, averaged over time, for one band-limited analytic-phase array of shape channels by samples.
observables: per-channel analytic phase after bandpass filtering, channels by samples, alpha band
wrapped inter-channel phase differences in channel-index order

operator.name: discrete gradient along the channel-index ordering
operator.identity_conditions: Discrete difference operator on a one-dimensional ordering of channels, applied to wrapped phase values. The identity is exact for the wrapped-difference definition only; no physical identity is claimed.

interpretation.proposed_interpretation: The origin-invariant charge-separation term identifies a cortical propagating wave.
assumptions: Channel-index order approximates spatial adjacency. The source module states that channel order does not encode geometry, so this assumption is unmet for any montage.
The Hilbert analytic phase after bandpass filtering reflects the narrow-band phase of the signal.
alternative_explanations: Volume conduction makes neighbouring channels phase-correlated without any circulation (Nolte et al. 2004; Stam et al. 2007).
Band-limited filtering and the Hilbert transform impose phase relations between channels that do not reflect a source process.
Channel labelling order is arbitrary, so the value can change under relabelling with no change in the recording.
confounds: Reference scheme (common average or single reference) shifts inter-channel phase differences.
Low signal-to-noise ratio flattens inter-channel phase differences toward uniform values.
Choice of frequency band (alpha, 8 to 13 Hz, from DEFAULT_EEG_BANDS).

falsifiers.test: Recompute phase_grad after a random permutation of channel order on identical recordings.
falsifiers.discriminates: If the value changes under permutation while the recording is unchanged, the metric reflects labelling order rather than spatial circulation, which falsifies the spatial reading.

falsifiers.test: Compare observed values with phase-randomised surrogates that preserve each channel's amplitude spectrum.
falsifiers.discriminates: If observed values fall within the surrogate distribution, the feature carries no structure beyond linear spectral content, which falsifies the proposed reading.

falsifiers.test: Repeat the comparison with a volume-conduction-robust pairwise measure, such as the phase lag index, on identical data.
falsifiers.discriminates: If the effect disappears under the robust measure, the reading is confounded by shared sources, which falsifies it.

empirical_claim.statement: If the channel-index phase gradient tracks inter-channel phase circulation, its magnitude should differ between conditions that differ in circulation.
empirical_claim.required_data: Recordings from at least two declared conditions and a locked analysis plan. This contract accesses no data.
empirical_claim.analysis_design: Compare the feature across the declared conditions against phase-randomised surrogates and a volume-conduction-robust pairwise measure, under one locked contrast.
controls: phase-randomised surrogates that preserve amplitude spectra

construct_validity.basis: No empirical data was analyzed. A computable descriptor does not establish that it measures the intended construct.

not_established: Does not establish that EEG electrodes are literal gauge or quantum objects. The operator is imported as a signal-processing generator only.
Does not establish that phase_grad measures phase circulation or any spatial topology. Channel-index order is not geometry.
Does not establish a causal or mechanistic relation, empirical support, or a scientific pass.
Does not compute a formal Bayes factor and assigns no evidence state. The claim gate's decision is recorded by reference only.
